description: Single-panel line-and-marker plot carrying three y-axes. The x-axis holds three categorical conditions: As-cast 0Cr, As-cast 6Cr and Annealed 6Cr. The left black y-axis (0-120, ticks every 30) is slip band spacing in nm; the right magenta axis (0-25, ticks every 5) is slip band width in nm; the right blue axis (0-50, ticks every 10) is total elongation in %. The legend prints all three entries exactly: "Slip bands spacing (nm)" (black filled squares), "Slip bands width (nm)" (magenta filled triangles) and "Total elongation (%)" (blue open circles). Slip band spacing decreases monotonically: As-cast 0Cr sits just below the 90 gridline, As-cast 6Cr about midway between the 60 and 90 gridlines, and Annealed 6Cr on the 60 gridline. Slip band width also decreases, from between the 10 and 15 nm ticks (As-cast 0Cr) to about 12.5 nm (As-cast 6Cr) and then to just under 8 nm (Annealed 6Cr). Total elongation is lowest for As-cast 6Cr (near the 30% gridline), intermediate for As-cast 0Cr (upper thirties) and highest for Annealed 6Cr (just above 40%). The figure demonstrates that finer slip bands with smaller spacing accompany the highest ductility except for as-cast 6Cr, whose elongation is the lowest. No numeric data labels are printed on the plot.

observations.observation: The plot uses three simultaneous y-axes: left black axis for slip band spacing (0-120, ticks every 30), right magenta axis for slip band width (0-25, ticks every 5) and right blue axis for total elongation (0-50 %, ticks every 10).
The x-axis contains exactly three conditions: As-cast 0Cr, As-cast 6Cr and Annealed 6Cr; no annealed 0Cr condition is plotted.

Slip band spacing (black squares) decreases monotonically from just below the 90 nm gridline (As-cast 0Cr) to between the 60 and 90 nm gridlines (As-cast 6Cr) to exactly on the 60 nm gridline (Annealed 6Cr).
Slip band width (magenta triangles) decreases from between the 10 and 15 nm ticks for As-cast 0Cr, to about 12.5 nm for As-cast 6Cr, down to just below the 10 nm tick for Annealed 6Cr.
Total elongation (blue open circles) is lowest for As-cast 6Cr at about the 30 % gridline, higher for As-cast 0Cr (between 30 and 40 %), and highest for Annealed 6Cr (just above 40 %).
The legend entries are printed exactly as "Slip bands spacing (nm)", "Slip bands width (nm)" and "Total elongation (%)".
The caption states the figure shows slip band spacing and width after tensile fracture of 0Cr and 6Cr strips with different status.

The citing text states that average widths of slip bands in as-cast 0Cr and 6Cr strips are 13.4 nm and 12.5 nm, and in annealed 0Cr and 6Cr strips are 20.5 nm and 7.9 nm, respectively (attributed to Fig. 12 in the text).
The citing text states that the average width of slip bands is inversely correlated with spacing between slip bands after tensile fracture.

The citing text states that although κ-carbides in the as-cast 6Cr strip have the lowest content and smallest size of the three strips, its total elongation after tensile fracture is the lowest, attributed to its high dislocation density before stretching.

The three series in this figure move in the same direction for spacing and width (both decrease from As-cast 0Cr to Annealed 6Cr), while elongation is non-monotonic with a minimum at As-cast 6Cr, i.e. the inverse correlation between slip band width and spacing holds but does not track elongation for as-cast 6Cr.

subfigures.description: One multi-axis line plot (no panel letters): three series — slip band spacing (nm, left black axis 0-120), slip band width (nm, right magenta axis 0-25) and total elongation (%, right blue axis 0-50) — plotted against three x categories As-cast 0Cr, As-cast 6Cr and Annealed 6Cr, with a legend in the lower-left listing all three series.

unreadable_items: Exact numeric values of the data points are not printed as labels; only axis ticks are readable, so individual values can only be bounded by gridlines
